methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units of information. Each atomic unit represents a distinct requirement, feature, or behavior of the decade counter. The goal was to create independent, self-contained, technically specific, and unambiguous units that could be individually assessed for coverage and similarity. This involved identifying key functionalities (counting, resetting), constraints (synchronous reset, decade range), and structural elements (clock input, reset input, output register).
mindtraced_atomic_units: Resets the counter to 0 on the next rising clock edge when asserted
spec_atomic_units: clk: single-bit input representing the clock signal
reset: single-bit input representing the synchronous reset signal (active high)
q: 4-bit output register representing the current count value (0-9)
q is updated within an always block triggered by the clock signal
Implements a decade counter with a synchronous reset
If reset is asserted (high), the next state of q is forced to 0
If reset is not asserted, the logic determines whether to increment q or reset it to 0
A comparator checks if the current value of q is equal to 9
Based on the result of the comparison, the next state of q is either q + 1 (if q is less than 9) or 0 (if q is equal to 9)
The adder is only used to increment by 1, so a simplified incrementer circuit can be used instead of a full adder
The counter increments on the rising edge of clk
When reset is high, the counter q is reset to 0 on the next rising edge of clk
When reset is low, the counter increments on each rising edge of clk until it reaches 9, at which point it resets to 0 on the next rising edge of clk
The next state of q depends on the current state of q and the value of reset at the rising edge of clk
The counter's behavior is defined within an always @(posedge clk) block
The q register is updated using non-blocking assignments
The counter consists of a single 4-bit register q declared as output reg [3:0] q
